analysis.evidence: The verb names Abram as the speaker and introduces his question to יַהְוֶה, מַה תִּתֶּן לִי (“What will you give me?”).
analysis.morphology: The prefixed conjunction וַ introduces a Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, agreeing with אַבְרָם.

draft.change: Link the existing Abram article to אבה through its father element and add Genesis 12:4 as an example.
draft.definition: Abram, son of Terah, later named Abraham. The name means “exalted father.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 12:4 repeats the name אַבְרָם when giving Abram’s age at departure. The name’s אָב element belongs to Haqor’s אבה article.

analysis.evidence: וַיֹּאמֶּר אַבְרָם means “Abram said.” The name identifies the speaker who addresses the Lord and says he is childless.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Abram, the son of Terah later named Abraham

analysis.evidence: Abram addresses Yahweh as אֲדֹנָי יַהְוֶה and asks מַה תִּתֶּן לִי, “What will you give me?” The pointing אֲדֹנָי and the divine name identify the title, and the singular verb תִּתֶּן confirms that Abram addresses one listener.
analysis.morphology: Masculine plural construct noun with a first-person singular possessive suffix. The fixed form אֲדֹנָי functions here as a singular divine title in direct address.
analysis.sense: אֲדֹנָי as a title for God

analysis.evidence: Abram addresses God as אֲדֹנָי יַהְוֶה, “Lord Yahweh,” before asking מַה תִּתֶּן לִי, “What will you give me?” The name identifies the addressee.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun in direct address, with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Personal name of the God of Israel

analysis.evidence: In מַה תִּתֶּן לִי, “What will you give me?”, לִי identifies Abram as the recipient, and מַה asks what he will receive. Abram explains the question by saying that he is childless.
analysis.morphology: Uninflected interrogative pronoun with no prefix or suffix. It serves as the direct object of תִּתֶּן.

analysis.evidence: Abram asks מַה תִּתֶּן לִי, “What will you give me?” מַה asks what the gift will be, and לִי identifies Abram as its recipient. His childlessness explains the question.
analysis.morphology: Qal imperfect, second person masculine singular. Abram addresses Yahweh directly.
analysis.sense: give something to someone for their use

analysis.evidence: Abram says וְאָנֹכִי הוֹלֵךְ עֲרִירִי, “and I am going to my death childless.” His question about what God can give him leads directly to the prospect of Eliezer inheriting his household. This concern with succession supports reading הוֹלֵךְ as departure in death.
analysis.morphology: Qal active participle, masculine singular absolute, with no prefix or suffix. It serves as the predicate of אָנֹכִי, “I,” referring to Abram.

draft.change: Add the adjective עֲרִירִי under ערר with the sense “childless” and correct the occurrence gloss from “wolf” to “childless.”
draft.definition: עֲרִירִי describes someone who has no child of their own.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 15:2–3 Abram explains his condition by saying that he has been given no offspring.

analysis.evidence: Abram describes himself as עֲרִירִי and names Eliezer of his household. In Genesis 15:3 he explains that he has been given no offspring and that a member of his household will inherit from him.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew adjective, masculine singular absolute, describing Abram as he says אֲנֹכִי הוֹלֵךְ, “I go.” The final ־ִי belongs to the adjective. The word has no prefix or pronominal suffix.
analysis.sense: Having no child of one's own.

draft.change: Add Genesis 15:2 as an example of the existing ben-member sense.
draft.definition: In construct, one who belongs to the household or company named by the following expression.
draft.evidence: Genesis 15:2 identifies Eliezer through his connection to Abram’s house. Abram’s shorter expression בֶן־בֵּיתִי in Genesis 15:3 clarifies that connection while leaving the precise meaning of מֶשֶׁק open.

analysis.evidence: Abram calls himself עֲרִירִי, childless, and identifies the man described by בֶן מֶשֶׁק בֵּיתִי as Eliezer. In Genesis 15:3 he restates his concern with בֶן־בֵּיתִי, a member of my household, and says that this man will inherit from him. Household membership is the sense of בֶן here. The verb יוֹרֵשׁ in verse 3 supplies the expectation of inheritance.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וּ precedes בֶן, the masculine singular construct of בֵּן. The noun heads the construct chain בֶן מֶשֶׁק בֵּיתִי.
analysis.sense: A man identified by the household to which he belongs.

draft.change: Add a noun entry for מֶשֶׁק with a qualified household-management sense.
draft.definition: Probably the management of a household, in an expression designating its steward.
draft.evidence: Genesis 15:2 places מֶשֶׁק between בֶן and בֵּיתִי in Abram’s description of Eliezer. Genesis 15:3 explains why this household member matters to the childless Abram.

analysis.evidence: Abram identifies Eliezer as בֶן מֶשֶׁק בֵּיתִי, commonly understood as “the steward of my house.” In the next verse Abram calls his expected heir בֶן־בֵּיתִי, “a member of my household.” This clarifies Eliezer’s place in the household and his prospect of inheriting. The narrower meaning “management” for מֶשֶׁק itself is probable but uncertain.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state. It governs בֵּיתִי (“my house”) within the longer construct chain וּבֶן מֶשֶׁק בֵּיתִי.

analysis.evidence: הוּא links the household description בֶן מֶשֶׁק בֵּיתִי to the name דַּמֶּשֶׂק אֱלִיעֶזֶר, identifying the person Abram means.
analysis.morphology: Independent third-person masculine singular personal pronoun.
analysis.sense: is (in a clause without a verb)

draft.change: Add a place-name article keyed by the pointed lemma דַּמֶּשֶׂק. Its consonants דמשׂק distinguish it from the candidate root דמע.
draft.definition: Damascus, the city named as the capital of Aram.
draft.evidence: Genesis 14:15 locates Hobah relative to Damascus. Isaiah 7:8 identifies Damascus as the head of Aram.

analysis.evidence: Abram places דַּמֶּשֶׂק immediately before אֱלִיעֶזֶר. The place-name identifies Eliezer by his association with Damascus, conventionally rendered “Eliezer of Damascus.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: The city of Damascus, used to locate Hobah.

evidence.note: Abram names the man of his household דַּמֶּשֶׂק אֱלִיעֶזֶר, “Eliezer of Damascus.”
Moses explains his son’s name אֱלִיעֶזֶר with אֱלֹהֵי אָבִי בְּעֶזְרִי, “the God of my father was my help,” recalling his deliverance from Pharaoh’s sword.

article.name: אֱלִיעֶזֶר
article.summary: Abram names Eliezer of Damascus as a man of his household. The name combines אֱלִי, “my God,” with עֶזֶר, “help.” Moses explains the name of his own son Eliezer by recalling how his father’s God helped him.

draft.change: Add a personal-name article linking the divine element אֱלִי to אֵל and the element עֶזֶר to the root עזר.
draft.definition: Eliezer, a Hebrew personal name meaning “my God is help.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 15:2 identifies Eliezer of Damascus. Exodus 18:4 explains the same name for Moses’ son through the words “the God of my father was my help.”

analysis.evidence: Abram says he is childless and identifies the man of his household by name in הוּא דַּמֶּשֶׂק אֱלִיעֶזֶר, “he is Eliezer of Damascus.”
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name, written as one word with no attached prefix or suffix.
analysis.sense: Eliezer of Damascus, a man of Abram’s household
